name: Lacrimal Drainage System Anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Lacrimal Drainage System Anomalies

criteria.description: Persistent tearing (epiphora) from birth or early infancy
Palpable swelling over the lacrimal sac region indicating dacryocystocele or mucocele
Failure of lacrimal duct irrigation or probing confirming obstruction
Imaging evidence (dacryocystography or dacryoscintigraphy) of lacrimal drainage obstruction
No evidence of acute infection at presentation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistent epiphora plus either palpable lacrimal sac swelling or failure of lacrimal duct irrigation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical, supported by imaging and failure of lacrimal duct patency tests.

searchTerms: tear drainage obstruction present at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dacryocystocele presenting as medial canthal swelling
searchTerms: tear sac cyst causing inner eye swelling

occasional.symptomName: Mild facial asymmetry due to swelling
Secondary skin excoriation near medial canthus
searchTerms: skin sores near inner eye corner

rare.symptomName: Orbital cellulitis secondary to lacrimal infection
searchTerms: eye socket infection from tear duct
eye infection spreading from lacrimal gland
orbital infection due to tear duct

rare.symptomName: Systemic febrile illness related to infection

searchTerms: chronic tear sac infection with skin opening
long-term lacrimal sac infection with fistula
persistent tear duct infection with drainage

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers in cases of dacryocystitis
Microbial cultures from lacrimal sac discharge
imaging: Dacryocystography showing obstruction or dilation of lacrimal sac
Ultrasound of lacrimal sac revealing cystic dilation
Dacryoscintigraphy demonstrating delayed or absent drainage
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; mostly sporadic congenital anomalies
other: Clinical confirmation by failure of lacrimal duct irrigation or probing

distinguishingFeatures: Acute infection signs with pain and erythema
Complete absence or severe hypoplasia of nasolacrimal duct

redFlags: Rapidly increasing swelling with pain and erythema
Signs of orbital cellulitis (proptosis, restricted eye movement)
Systemic febrile illness indicating possible sepsis
references: Orphanet: Lacrimal drainage system anomaly - ORPHA:98605
